chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said:

The fur, the khuff, the cap, the turban, the belt, and the trousers are removed from the martyr, unless blood has affected them; if blood has affected them, they are left. And nothing tied is to be left upon him except that it is untied.

key_terms.الشَّهِيدِ: the martyr, whose body has special rulings after death
key_terms.الْفَرْوُ: a fur garment or outer covering
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood, which affects whether an item is left on the body

ai.seo_question: What clothing should be removed from a martyr, and what should remain on the body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the treatment of a martyr's body after death. It specifies which garments are removed, makes an exception for items stained with blood, and requires that any tied item be untied.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.446 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"From a martyr, the fur, shoes, cap, turban, belt, and trousers should be removed, unless they have been stained with blood ; if they are stained with blood, they are to be left on. No tied item should remain on the body; it must be untied."
